court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Mr. Ketan Netaji Sutar And Anr vs Smt. Surekha Netaji Sutar And Ors

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Ketan Netaji Sutar and others (husband, wife, plaintiff)
parties.respondent_defendant: Smt. Surekha Netaji Sutar and others (wife, children, defendant)

facts_of_case: Appellants claim to be the second wife of deceased who died in 2010. Appellant No.2 moved an application under Section 372 of Indian Succession Act for grant of a Succession Certificate. Respondent No.1 is the first and legally wedded wife of the deceased.

legal_principles.principle: A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus if neither party has a spouse living at the time of the marriage.
legal_principles.held: Section 5 (i) of Hindu Marriage Act contemplates; 'A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus, (i) neither party has a spouse living at the time of the marriage.'

legal_principles.principle: A document that is only a plain piece of paper on which parents and some other villagers had put their signatures cannot be accepted as an admissible evidence.
legal_principles.held: It cannot be accepted as an admissible evidence. Merely because the appellant No.2 and the deceased along with the respondents were staying under one roof, it cannot be said that appellant No.2 acquired a status of a legally wedded wife of the deceased.
cited_cases: Union of India and Anr. Vs. V. R. Tripathi

legal_principles.principle: A person claiming a job on compassionate ground due to the death of the deceased must establish their marriage with the deceased.
legal_principles.held: The question of solemnization of so called marriage of the appellant No.2 with the deceased is inconsequential. The applicant has failed to establish her marriage with the deceased.
cited_cases: Vijaya Ukarda Athor (Athawale) Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors.

outcome.final_order: The marriage of the deceased with appellant No.2 was declared void in view of Section 11 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
